learned: Price-only search cuts Star surplus to 1.41–2.23 but cannot meet 0.9–1.1. Low-demand/bot stockpiles dominate. Cosmetic costs high enough to absorb every grant risk blocking purchases. Next add a bounded Star bank that pauses new grants without deleting old stock, plus native progression diagnostics.
structure: Uses the E2 finite studio loadout and exact production quotes; recipes cannot buy a roll or create unfunded burns.

title: Bounded weekly grants
learned: The bank cap reduces Star accumulation substantially, but a capped bank must still afford every recipe. Escalating showcase Thread costs force the bank too high; next test a fixed Thread fitting cost, low-cap sampling, and native recorded item quality. Bot efficiency and late guaranteed tailoring remain separate misses.

title: Recorded quality and valid low banks
learned: Use actual native item rolls and completed-route rewards; eliminate historical quality reconstruction for this bank. Fixed Thread cost per showcase shelf permits smaller banks. Guaranteed tailoring remains the progression bottleneck in this bank. Next use the separately measured faster v3 recipe and allow one-Thread recipes so the lowest bank can afford every action.

title: One-Thread reserve and faster tailoring
learned: The native progression pilot now meets casual/heavy median day targets, and burn medians pass. A one-Thread bank still has up to 16.5% surplus because expensive polish competes for limited wallets. Next lower guaranteed-polish and decor YARN ranges. The config key-order recovery is verified against every original worker hash; this round had two global passes, with no local refinement claimed.

title: Lower priced one-Thread crafts
learned: Cheaper polish reduces unspent Thread, but finite collections and churn still leave reserves above the target in some scenarios. Progression remains in range. Next inspect actual reward eligibility and voluntary spending timing; lowering prices alone cannot fix repetitive farming efficiency.

title: Affordable one-Thread reserve
learned: All median and p90 targets except bot efficiency pass in the 40-seed search. The worst Thread ratio is 1.0966, very close to 1.10, so next broaden the reward split and test lower fusion costs without raising the bank. Bots stop at the reward cap: no unused AFK hours are counted. No final acceptance is claimed from this pilot.

title: Reward split and cheaper quality steps
learned: 29 of 40 candidates satisfy burn, Thread and progression targets in the pilot. The best has Thread 1.0392–1.0935 but last-quarter burn can fall to 0.9861 even while annual burn passes. Next stress seal/fusion prices and low withdrawal caps; retain annual and last-quarter results separately. Higher weekly rewards did not solve bot efficiency.

title: Seal prices and withdrawal caps
learned: With 40 native seeds, the best candidate passes T-a/b/c/d/f/g and puts Thread at 1.0285–1.0807. Annual burn reaches only 1.026 at the low end, and last-quarter burn falls to 0.9732. Bot efficiency remains 0.91–0.93; withdrawal caps do not identify automation. Next use the completed 200-seed native bank and emphasize a lower payout range with affordable real sinks.

title: Completed 200-seed native bank
learned: The best of 40 configs on the verified 200-seed native bank still misses: burn/claims 0.9642-1.5165, Star source/sink 1.0481-1.1094, bot/human active-hour efficiency 0.8998-0.9467. Casual Legendary remains day 13 and heavy 8.5-9. Lower the high rank bonus and skin/fusion prices while exploring a small Thread buffer; do not invent a bot-only reward multiplier.

title: Balance low-Star source caps and affordable sinks
learned: The 200-seed native bank preserves casual day 13 and heavy day 9 progression. This round tests reduced weekly grants, one-to-three Star bank caps, and cheaper repeatable sinks across 17 levers; bot hourly efficiency still needs a structural earning rule and no E3 acceptance is claimed.

title: Withdrawal cap and affordable recurring sinks
learned: Narrowing weekly claim caps, rank grants, and recurring sink prices slightly worsened the worst-case score versus round 10 (5.8939 vs 5.8654). Bot efficiency remains structurally too close to human efficiency; price-only tuning cannot close T-e. Preserve both candidate sets for final Pareto confirmation.

title: Bound Star accumulation and make low-cost sinks reachable
learned: The low bank cap plus cheaper Star-consuming upgrades brings all 18 median Star ratios to 1.039-1.097 while burn/claims stays 1.034-1.521. Bot/human hourly earnings remains 0.916-0.961; a structural participation change is still required. This is 40-seed evidence, not final confirmation.

title: Wider claim and sink affordability bounds
learned: The wider ranges improve the aggregate score to 5.8084 but let worst-case median Star source/sink rise to 1.122. Burn/claims spans 1.018-1.571 and bot/human hourly earnings 0.908-0.955. Retain round12 as the stronger Star-balanced candidate; the bot gate still needs a structural earning rule.

title: Keep one Thread in reserve and tune earning bounds
learned: The one-Thread bank and adjusted weekly grants improve score to5.7756. Record the full scenario results and use them to tighten round15; no bot-efficiency acceptance is claimed. Native progression is unchanged from the200-seed bank.

title: Lower grants with affordable repeat sinks
learned: Reducing weekly Spool to 0.25–0.60 worsened the best score to 6.3276. Burn/claims spans 1.0035–1.6523, Star source/sink 1.0565–1.1227, and bot/human hourly earnings 0.9032–0.9485. Round12 remains stronger. Next narrow around its affordable sink prices and weekly supply; a structural earning rule is still needed for bots.

title: Local supply and sink refinement
learned: Refining round12 yields score 5.7086; median ranges: burnClaims [1.0083, 1.5089], starRatio [1.0527, 1.1242], botRegularHourlyRatio [0.8985, 0.9511].
